acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Deep Ones family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Deep Priest, T4, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Pressure-Organ Champion (Champion) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two wind construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Tentacular beard and jaw growths, pressure-scarred plating, translucent skin with glowing organs, and whale-bone staff.
Signature mechanic: Organ Litany: one visible organ fills, the matching jaw tentacle grips a staff notch, and a pressure-scarred plate seals the selected zone.
battlefieldDuty: Control alternating zones by exposing source-supported translucent organs and routing pressure through jaw tentacles into a whale-bone staff.
constructionDimensions: Tier-safe anatomy: T1–T2 have no lure, no tentacles, no translucent organs, no kraken limbs, and no crown; T3 alone first gains its lure; T4 first gains tentacles and translucent organs; T5 alone gains kraken limbs and crown.
Directional fin vanes, net streamers, gill pressure flutes, debris vectors, and a still throat between pulses create readable force distinct from ordinary sea movement.
counterplay: Move to the dim-organ flank and sever the gripping tentacle after the zone releases. Affinity signal: Tier-safe anchors: T1–T2 have no lure, no tentacles, no translucent organs, no kraken limbs, and no crown, so the still gill-neck opens between gusts; T3 lure marks the pressure lane; T4 tentacles and translucent organs reveal the still organ; T5 kraken limbs and crown expose the commanded calm anchor.
forbiddenTreatments: Floating anatomy that loses ground contact
identityInvariants: Hunched long-armed humanoid silhouette, wide flat head, lidless eyes, gill-neck, fins, webbed claws, and needle teeth remain legible.
Drowned green, deep-sea blue-black, sickly grey, pearlescent white, and bounded cold native light form the source palette.
Wet scale, eel skin, coral, barnacle, driftwood, rusted metal, whale bone, net, pearl, and shell remain distinct materials.
Pressure bulk, loss of familiar humanoid proportion, and native light-bearing anatomy escalate at explicit source tiers.
telegraph: A translucent organ brightens while one beard tentacle coils around a whale-bone notch.
